candidates.source_name: Athanasius of Alexandria / Orationes contra Arianos II.13
candidates.source_attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Orationes contra Arianos (Four Discourses Against the Arians, I-IV), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 26 (1857).
candidates.draft_body:
Athanasius of Alexandria Orationes contra Arianos II.13 (c. 350 AD)

'Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever: the sceptre of thy kingdom is a right sceptre' (LXX 44:7 — ho thronos sou ho theos eis ton aiōna tou aiōnos) — Athanasius marks Ps 45:6 (LXX 44:7) as the DIRECT VOCATIVE-ADDRESS of the Son as ho theos (the-God, with definite article). The Father is the speaker; the Son the addressee; the address is unambiguous in the vocative-with-article. The author of Hebrews (1:8) cites this verse against the angels — 'unto which of the angels said he at any time...' (1:5) and culminates with this 'But unto the Son he saith, Thy throne, O God' — Athanasius treats Heb 1:8's citation as the canonical apostolic-warrant for reading Ps 45:6's vocative as direct-Trinitarian-address, not metaphor or hypostatized-attribute.
candidates.reviewer_notes: Curated PD interpretive summary representing the Ethiopian Tewahedo tradition's reading via Athanasius of Alexandria, Orationes contra Arianos II.13.
